solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Flood defence completed following Depression (8)

blocks.note: f. is the standard abbreviation for following
a low is a weather depression

annotation.surface: A news line about a sea wall finished after a stormy spell.
annotation.walkthrough: Depression looks like the storm the defence was built for, but it is the weather low that ends the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An overflow is the channel or pipe that carries off excess water so a tank or reservoir does not flood.

entries.clue: Old ways in which soldiers brought back commands (6)

indicatorNotes.in which: the soldiers sit inside the ways
indicatorNotes.brought back: the soldiers are turned round before going in

blocks.note: rds = roads; ER goes between RD and S
RE = Royal Engineers, turned to ER

annotation.surface: A history of how old regiments received their instructions.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pushes soldiers taking commands back to base; in the wordplay the soldiers are the Royal Engineers, a stock crossword unit, and they are what gets brought back.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: commands and orders are both instructions a superior issues.

entries.clue: On a high with my boss coming around in the early hours (6)

indicatorNotes.coming around: the boss goes round the other piece

blocks.note: the editor is a newspaper setter's boss; E…D
out in the small hours is out late

annotation.surface: Someone buzzing because the boss has dropped round in the middle of the night.
annotation.walkthrough: My boss is ED, the editor, from the setter's point of view as a newspaper contributor.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: being on a high is feeling euphoric, the same state as being thrilled and overjoyed.

entries.clue: Jellied eggs somehow go with prawns, fine as a starter (9)

indicatorNotes.somehow: the letters are put together in some other way
indicatorNotes.as a starter: only the first letter of fine is taken

blocks.note: first letter of fine, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A restaurant starter of jellied eggs with prawns, a fine way to begin.
annotation.walkthrough: The menu surface makes jellied eggs sound like a starter; they are the eggs of frogs.
annotation.definitionFit: Frogspawn is the mass of frogs' eggs set in jelly.

entries.clue: One often opening doors for an Eton man? (3,6,3)

annotation.definition: One often opening doors for an Eton man?

blocks.note: read as a doorman or footman, and meant as a connection that opens doors to jobs and clubs
on the surface the person being let in; in the answer the wearer of the school's neckwear

annotation.surface: A servant or doorman holding doors for an Old Etonian.
annotation.walkthrough: The doors are careers, not house doors: the old school tie stands for the network of former pupils who help each other on.
annotation.definitionFit: An old school tie, worn by ex-pupils of a public school like Eton, is shorthand for the favours that network does its members.

entries.clue: Good turn-over dessert off the menu? (4,2)

indicatorNotes.turn-over: the pudding is turned over, end to end

annotation.surface: A turnover pastry pudding that the restaurant has run out of.
annotation.walkthrough: A turnover is a real pastry dessert, which hides the instruction to turn PUD over.
annotation.definitionFit: A dish off the menu has been used up, with none left to serve.

entries.clue: Coach returning to pick up personnel in plant (5)

indicatorNotes.returning: a coach returning drives back the way it came, so its letters are read in the opposite direction
indicatorNotes.to pick up: the reversed coach takes the personnel on board, inside it

blocks.note: a coach is a bus; reversed SUB, as SU…B
HR = human resources, the personnel department

annotation.surface: A coach going back to collect workers at a factory.
annotation.walkthrough: Plant reads as a factory for the staff, but it is the definition: a bush.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a bush is one kind of plant, the woody, many-stemmed kind smaller than a tree.

entries.clue: Scottish banker wins small house in draw (8)

indicatorNotes.wins: the river takes, and holds, the pieces that follow

blocks.note: the Dee is a Scottish river, something with banks; DE…E

annotation.surface: A Scottish bank employee wins a little house in a prize draw.
annotation.walkthrough: A banker in crosswords is often a river, which has banks. Draw means depict, not a lottery.
annotation.definitionFit: To draw a picture or a line in words is to describe it.

entries.clue: Line out of standard vintage songs and burlesques (8)

indicatorNotes.out of: the line is taken out of the songs

blocks.note: L = line, removed from OLDIES to leave ODIES

annotation.surface: A cabaret programme of old standards, classic songs and burlesque acts.
annotation.walkthrough: Standard and vintage songs sound like one music-hall list; standard is golf's PAR.
annotation.definitionFit: Burlesques are mocking imitations, which is what parodies are.

entries.clue: Suit of ice (8)

blocks.note: one of the four suits in a pack of cards
underworld slang for cut gems, from their cold glitter

annotation.surface: A suit made of ice.
annotation.walkthrough: Ice is slang for diamonds, from their cold glitter.
annotation.definitionFit: Diamonds are one of the four card suits, and ice is underworld slang for diamonds.

entries.clue: Some massager — a serious rubber (6)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters of the next words are used

annotation.surface: A masseur who kneads with real force.
annotation.walkthrough: Rubber means one who rubs in the surface, but here it is the thing that rubs out pencil.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in British English a rubber is the block used to rub out pencil marks.

entries.clue: Rash types rush all over the shop with a mum’s car (5-7)

annotation.surface: Reckless shoppers charging around a store, one of them in mum's car.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator doubles as the surface's picture of people careering round a shop.
annotation.definitionFit: Harum-scarums are reckless, impetuous people.

entries.clue: Grasses Blunt and Philby etc crossed England (5)

indicatorNotes.crossed: the spies lie across England, enclosing it

blocks.note: Anthony Blunt and Kim Philby were Soviet spies, communists: RE…DS

annotation.surface: Informers betraying the Cambridge spies Blunt and Philby, who double-crossed England.
annotation.walkthrough: Grasses reads as informers, which fits a clue about spies, but it is the plant. Blunt and Philby were Cambridge-educated Britons who spied for the Soviet Union.
annotation.definitionFit: Reeds are tall grasses that grow in wet ground.

entries.clue: Loaded, having loads of rooms? (9)

blocks.note: of a gun, with a cartridge put into the chamber
a chamber is a room, so the word read literally means full of them

annotation.surface: Rich, and living in a house with lots of rooms.
annotation.walkthrough: Loaded suggests wealth, which suits a big house, but it means a gun with a round chambered.
annotation.definitionFit: A chambered cartridge is loaded in the gun, and something chambered is divided into chambers, rooms.

entries.clue: Brave on a mule travelling about Mobile (12)

indicatorNotes.travelling about: something travelling about roams from place to place, so the letters wander out of their order

annotation.surface: A plucky rider journeying on a mule around Mobile, Alabama.
annotation.walkthrough: Mobile has a capital M so it looks like the Alabama city, but the capital is only the first word's.
annotation.definitionFit: Something manoeuvrable can be moved about easily: it is mobile.

entries.clue: Clergyman missing final church worship (9)

indicatorNotes.missing final: the clergyman loses his last letter

blocks.note: a reverend, minus its last letter D, leaves REVEREN

annotation.surface: A vicar who skips the last church service.
annotation.walkthrough: Final looks like it goes with church worship, but it takes the last letter off the clergyman.
annotation.definitionFit: Reverence is deep respect, and to worship is to revere.
annotation.definitionNote: worship is read as a noun here, deep veneration

entries.clue: Just horrible giving leading female the boot (8)

indicatorNotes.giving leading female the boot: the first letter, F for female, is kicked out

blocks.note: F = female, the leading letter, removed

annotation.surface: Only a dreadful act, sacking the lead actress.
annotation.walkthrough: Just reads as merely, but it is the adjective: fair and proper.
annotation.definitionFit: Rightful means just, legitimate, as in a rightful heir.

entries.clue: Stingy type of heir limiting men with power (8)

indicatorNotes.limiting: the heir sets the limits either side of the other pieces

blocks.note: a scion is a descendant, an heir: SC…ION

annotation.surface: A mean young heir keeping powerful men on a short leash.
annotation.walkthrough: Stingy looks like mean, a miser; read it as having a sting.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: stingy is read as sting-bearing, and this arachnid carries a venomous sting at the tip of its tail.

entries.clue: In Barking, vice-consul gets unsettled (12)

indicatorNotes.Barking: barking means mad, so the letters are crazed

annotation.surface: A diplomat posted to Barking, in east London, feels restless.
annotation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London, which makes In Barking look like a place; barking is also British slang for mad.
annotation.definitionFit: A matter left unsettled is inconclusive, with no decision reached.

entries.clue: One spotted in party is old minister (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the minister goes inside the party and old

blocks.note: O = old; DO + O, split as DO…O

annotation.surface: Someone seen at a party turns out to be a former government minister.
annotation.walkthrough: One spotted reads as someone noticed, but it is a tile marked with spots.
annotation.definitionFit: A domino is a tile marked with spots.

entries.clue: Minister in a race gets to finish (6)

blocks.note: the TT, the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race

annotation.surface: A politician running in a race manages to cross the line.
annotation.walkthrough: Minister is a verb here: to minister to someone is to look after them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to minister to the sick is to look after and care for them.

entries.clue: Music producer hurt over in eastern California (9)

indicatorNotes.eastern: read from the east, right to left, IN runs backwards

annotation.surface: A record producer injured somewhere in the east of California.
annotation.walkthrough: Eastern California sounds like a region; eastern tells you to read IN from its east end.
annotation.definitionFit: A harmonica, or mouth organ, is an instrument, something that produces music.

entries.clue: Further trouble following Brexit! (5)

indicatorNotes.following Brexit!: after B (Britain) exits, it is gone

blocks.note: the first letter of Brexit, standing for Britain, exits BOTHER

annotation.surface: A grumble that Brexit has only brought more trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: Brexit is Britain's exit from the EU, so the clue has B leave the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Further, as in further details, means other, additional.

entries.clue: Aussie skippers finally inspect Harrier crash site (5)

indicatorNotes.finally: only the last letter of inspect is used

annotation.surface: Australian pilots finally inspect the site where a Harrier jump jet came down.
annotation.walkthrough: Harrier looks like the jet and crash like an accident; a harrier is a bird of prey and to crash is slang for going to sleep.
annotation.definitionFit: A roost is where a bird such as a harrier settles to sleep, or crashes.

entries.clue: Fleeing battle (had a fill of killing essentially) (6)

indicatorNotes.had a fill of: the battle is filled with the next piece
indicatorNotes.essentially: only the essence, the middle letter, of killing

annotation.surface: Running from a battle after having had enough of the slaughter.
annotation.walkthrough: Had a fill of reads as had enough of; it tells you to fill FIGHT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the noun sense: running away from danger, as in to take flight.
annotation.definitionNote: Fleeing is read as a noun, the act of running away

entries.clue: Cute icon given makeover failed to impress (3,2,3)

indicatorNotes.given makeover: the letters are made over into a new form

annotation.surface: A pretty celebrity got a makeover that nobody liked.
annotation.walkthrough: The makeover is literal: the same eight letters rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: an argument that makes no impression on someone is said to have had no effect on them at all.

entries.clue: Vessels left by those eating no starter (6)

indicatorNotes.by: left sits beside the next piece
indicatorNotes.no starter: the diners lose their first letter

blocks.note: diners, minus the D, leave INERS

annotation.surface: Plates left behind by diners who skipped the first course.
annotation.walkthrough: Vessels and starter suggest dishes at a meal; the vessels are ships.
annotation.definitionFit: Liners are large passenger ships, vessels.

entries.clue: A drug rock (8)

blocks.note: a class of drug, anabolic kinds used by bodybuilders

annotation.surface: Drug slang: rock is a street name for crack cocaine.
annotation.walkthrough: Rock is a slang word for crack cocaine, so A drug rock reads as one phrase; the rock is in space.
annotation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a rocky body orbiting the sun.
